name: vault_info
description: Return where the currently configured ZenNotes vault lives (a folder on this machine, or a self-hosted server the desktop app is connected to) and its top-level layout. Call this once at the start of a session to confirm you are pointing at the right vault, and to learn whether the user runs in `inbox` or `root` primary mode (the answer changes how every other tool behaves).

name: list_notes
description: List notes in the vault with metadata (title, folder, tags, wikilinks, excerpt, timestamps). Optional filters narrow by folder, tag, or wikilink target. Use this before editing to pick the right note. Trashed notes are included only when folder='trash' is explicit. The returned `path` field is the canonical reference: pass it back verbatim to read_note / write_note / move_note. In `primaryNotesLocation: root` vaults, inbox notes have a path WITHOUT an `inbox/` prefix (e.g. `MyNote.md`); never add one. Each note also carries `link`, a clickable zennotes-rs:// URL that opens it in the app; use it verbatim when rendering note titles as markdown links for the user.

folder.description: Only return notes in this top-level folder.

subpath.description: POSIX subpath under the folder (e.g. "Work/Meetings"). Requires folder to be set.

tag.description: Only return notes that contain this #tag. Notes in the vault’s template folder are left out.

wikilinkTo.description: Only return notes that link to a note with this title.

updatedSinceMs.description: Only return notes updated at or after this epoch millisecond timestamp.

limit.description: Cap the number of notes returned. Default: 200.

name: list_folders
description: List every subfolder in the vault grouped by top-level folder.

name: list_assets
description: List the vault’s attachments: every file that is not a note, wherever it is (images, PDFs, audio, video, other binaries). Useful when a note references an asset you need to inspect. With deleted: true, lists the attachments in the app's Trash instead, with the undoToken restore_asset takes.

name: read_note
description: Read the full body and metadata of a single note. Always read before you write. Use the path verbatim from list_notes / search_* / create_note. Never invent or prefix it.

path.description: Vault-relative POSIX path exactly as another tool returned it. In `primaryNotesLocation: root` vaults this looks like "MyNote.md"; in `inbox` mode it looks like "inbox/MyNote.md". Pass it through unchanged.

name: write_note
description: Overwrite the full body of an existing note. Destructive, so prefer append_to_note / replace_in_note for incremental edits. Keep frontmatter intact unless the user asked you to change it.

name: create_note
description: Create a new note. Always picks a non-conflicting filename by appending a counter if needed. Use the `path` from the response to refer to the note in any follow-up tool calls. DO NOT reconstruct it from `folder + title`. In root-mode vaults, `folder: "inbox"` means the note lands directly at the vault root with a path like "MyNote.md" (no inbox/ prefix).

folder.description: Conceptual folder. Refuses "trash". In `primaryNotesLocation: inbox` vaults, "inbox" maps to <root>/inbox/; in `primaryNotesLocation: root` vaults, "inbox" maps to the vault root itself. quick/ and archive/ are always real subdirectories. Default if omitted: "inbox".

title.description: Human-readable title. Becomes the filename (sanitized). Optional; defaults to "Untitled".

subpath.description: POSIX subpath under the folder. Example: "Work/Research". Missing parents are created.

name: rename_note
description: Rename a note in place (filename only, same folder). Check backlinks() first so you can warn the user about dangling wikilinks.

name: move_note
description: Move a note to a new folder or subfolder. Use archive_note/unarchive_note/move_to_trash for the special destinations rather than this tool.

targetSubpath.description: Optional POSIX subpath under the folder.

name: duplicate_note
description: Duplicate a note next to itself with a " copy" suffix.

name: move_to_trash
description: Soft-delete: move the note into trash/. Reversible via restore_from_trash.

name: restore_from_trash
description: Restore a trashed note back to inbox/.

name: empty_trash
description: Permanently delete every note in trash/. Confirm with the user before calling: this is irreversible.

confirm.description: Must be true. Prevents accidental triggers.

name: delete_note
description: Permanently delete a single note file. Prefer move_to_trash unless the user explicitly asked for a hard delete.

name: archive_note
description: Move a note into archive/.

name: unarchive_note
description: Move an archived note back to inbox/.

name: create_folder
description: Create a subfolder under inbox/, quick/, or archive/.

name: rename_folder
description: Rename or move a subfolder in place.

name: delete_folder
description: Delete a subfolder and everything inside it. Destructive. Confirm with the user first.

name: search_text
description: Full-text search across live notes (inbox/quick/archive), leaving out the vault’s template folder. Returns line-level matches with path, line number, and preview. Cheap first step when the user says "find" or "where did I write".

name: search_by_title
description: Fuzzy-match notes by title (case-insensitive substring). Good for "open my note about …".

name: search_by_tag
description: Find notes carrying a specific inline #tag. Tags are case-insensitive; pass the name with or without the leading #. Notes in the vault’s template folder are left out.

name: list_tags
description: Enumerate every #tag used in the vault (excluding trash and the template folder) with the count of notes carrying it.

name: backlinks
description: Return every note that links to the given note via [[wikilink]]. Run this before renaming a note: the rename will orphan these links.

path.description: Vault-relative path to the target note.

name: list_tasks
description: Return every task (markdown checkbox) in live notes with parsed metadata: due date, priority, @waiting, tags, and status, the column a Kanban board grouped by status shows it in (a task note’s `status:`, a line’s `@status:`, or the frontmatter `status:` of its note). Filter by state, priority, date range, tag, or folder.

status.description: The task’s state, not its status column. open = not done, cancelled or waiting (default). done = checked. waiting = has @waiting. all = everything.

tags.description: Alternative to tag: require ALL of these tags.

includeExcluded.description: Also scan notes opted out of Tasks (frontmatter `tasks: false` / `tasks: note`), folders on the vault's excluded list, its template folder, and notes outside its Task folders. Default false: excluded tasks are invisible.

name: toggle_task
description: Flip a task’s checkbox state using its id from list_tasks ("<path>#<index>"). An id counts the task’s position in its note, so list_tasks again after that note changes. Finishing a task with `@repeat:` writes its next occurrence above it and returns the finished one under its new id. Returns the updated task, or null if the id no longer matches a task.

name: append_to_note
description: Append markdown to the end of a note (inserts a blank line separator if needed). Preferred for adding entries to daily logs, running lists, meeting notes.

text.description: Markdown to append (no leading newline needed).

name: prepend_to_note
description: Insert markdown at the top of a note, after any frontmatter block. Good for "pin this to the top" or adding a banner.

name: insert_at_line
description: Insert text before a given zero-based line number. Line numbers come from read_note or list_tasks (which reports lineNumber).

name: replace_in_note
description: Literal (non-regex) find-and-replace inside a single note. Returns the number of replacements made. Default scope: first occurrence.

name: list_comments
description: The comment threads on a note: each top-level comment with the text it is anchored to, the line that text sits on now, who wrote it (author is null for the vault owner), and its replies in order. Read this before reviewing or answering a discussion; unresolved threads only unless include_resolved is true.

include_resolved.description: Also list resolved threads. Default false.

name: add_comment
description: Start a new comment thread on a note, attributed to you. Pass anchor_text, a passage copied exactly from the note, to attach the comment to it (the app highlights it and jumps there); omit it for a note-level comment. Markdown is fine in the body. Returns the new thread.

anchor_text.description: Text from the note the comment is about, verbatim. Omit for a note-level comment.

author.description: Display name to sign with. Defaults to the connected client (e.g. "Claude Code").

name: reply_to_comment
description: Answer a comment in its thread, attributed to you. id is a thread id (or any reply id in it) from list_comments; the reply keeps the thread’s anchor. Use this to respond to the user’s comments the way you would on a pull request, instead of editing the note body. Returns the updated thread.

author.description: Display name to sign with. Defaults to the connected client.

name: resolve_comment
description: Mark a comment thread resolved (or reopen it with resolved: false). Resolve only when the discussion is settled or the user asks; the thread stays in the note’s history and moves to the Resolved section of the app’s Comments panel.

resolved.description: false reopens the thread. Default true.

name: read_asset
description: Read an attachment from list_assets: an image comes back as an image you can see, text as text, anything else (PDF, audio, video) as an embedded file. Files up to 5 MiB.

path.description: Vault-relative path exactly as list_assets returned it.

name: upload_asset
description: Add a file to the vault's assets folder from base64 (up to 16 MiB), never overwriting: a taken name gets a number. Returns its `path` and `markdown`, the embed or link to paste into a note with append_to_note or edit_section.

filename.description: File name with its extension, such as plot.png.

name: rename_asset
description: Rename an attachment in place. Notes that embed or link it are updated to the new name; `linksNotUpdated` lists any it could not read or write, which may still use the old name, so fix those by hand. Names holding # ? | [ ] ^ or % are refused, since links could not reach the file.

name.description: New file name with its extension, no folder.

name: move_asset
description: Move an attachment to another folder, creating it if needed. Notes that embed or link it are updated; `linksNotUpdated` lists any it could not read or write, which may still use the old name. A taken name gets a number, so use the returned `path`.

name: duplicate_asset
description: Copy an attachment next to itself with a " copy" suffix.

name: delete_asset
description: Soft-delete an attachment: it leaves the vault for the app's Trash and restore_asset brings it back. Keep the returned undoToken. Notes keep their links to it, so check them first with search_text.

name: restore_asset
description: Bring back a deleted attachment to where it was, using the undoToken from delete_asset or list_assets with deleted: true. A taken name gets a number, so use the returned `path`.

name: update_task
description: Change a task by its id from list_tasks: due date, priority, @waiting, state, status (Kanban column) or text. Only what you pass changes; pass "" to clear due, priority or status. The task stays where it is, and the rest of the note keeps its bytes, except that state done on a task with `@repeat:` writes its next occurrence above it, as toggle_task does, and returns the finished one. An id counts the task's position in its note, so pass expectedText to be told when an edit moved it. On a task note, state, status and waiting are one field: pass only one. Returns the updated task, or null if the id no longer matches one.

status.description: The column a Kanban board groups it under, one word, or "" to clear.

text.description: Replaces everything after the checkbox, one line, due and priority tokens included. Not for a task note: use rename_note.

expectedText.description: The task's content from list_tasks. If it no longer reads this, nothing changes and the call fails.

name: daily_note
description: Find the daily note for a date (or the weekly or monthly note holding it) under this vault's own folder and naming settings, which you cannot guess. Changes nothing. If `exists`, use its `path`. If not, pass `createWith` to create_note as it is, which starts the note from the vault's template, and use the `path` create_note returns. `cannotCreate` means this assistant may not create it. `enabled: false` means the user has this kind of note turned off, so ask before creating one.

date.description: today, yesterday, tomorrow or YYYY-MM-DD. Default: today.

name: note_sections
description: Read a note by its headings. Without `heading`: its outline, every heading with its level and lines, for long notes and for finding where to edit. With `heading`: the text under that heading, subheadings included, so you need not read the whole note. Lines are zero-based, as in insert_at_line; endLineNumber is exclusive.

heading.description: Heading text, any case, without the #s.

lineNumber.description: The heading's line, from the outline, when its text appears more than once.

name: edit_section
description: Edit the part of a note under one heading: `append` (the usual choice, such as a new item under Action Items; it goes above any subheading), `prepend`, or `replace`, which rewrites everything under the heading, subheadings included. The heading and the rest of the note keep their text. Fails with the note's headings if there is no such heading.

heading.description: Heading text, any case, without the #s.

text.description: Markdown. Empty only with replace, to clear the section.

lineNumber.description: The heading's line, from note_sections, when its text appears more than once.
